parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Wien’s displacement law. Identify any symbols that you use.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A cosmology student observes the electromagnetic radiation received from a star in a galaxy. The student uses Wien’s law to estimate the surface temperature of the star, a standard candle to estimate the distance to the galaxy, and the Stefan–Boltzmann law to estimate the radius of the star.

The student observes that the radiation from the star is redshifted.
parts.text: State what is meant by a standard candle.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the reason why the radiation from the star is redshifted.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The true values of the quantities observed or estimated are those that are corrected to allow for redshift. However, the student does not correct for redshift.

By placing one tick (✓) in each row, complete Table 10.1 to indicate how the observations and estimates made by the student compare with the true values.

figures.caption: Table 10.1
figures.alt: A table with columns for the student’s uncorrected value being too low, the same, or too high, and rows for wavelength of radiation, surface temperature of star, distance to star, and radius of star.
